I farm the way I know best: steady, practical, and not too risky. I am 68, and my family has only 2 people, so I will not make the work too complicated. I already know wheat and maize well, and with well irrigation I can keep the main wheat-maize land stable. That is where I will put most of my land, because it gives me grain in two seasons and feels safer. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I have grown it for many years and I do not want to give it up completely, but I will not expand it because cotton takes more management and more picking labor. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, give moderate fertilizer instead of pushing too hard, irrigate enough for my well-water conditions, and use rotary tillage because it saves labor and matches my age and farm size. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible yield; it is to keep the farm manageable, control costs, and get a reliable harvest from each crop.
